trust_decision.summary: The generator decides that a description or deprecation reason taken from an untrusted GraphQL schema may be interpolated verbatim into generated JSDoc; the missing decision is to encode the comment terminator before writing it, decided only in the shared comment builder at cli/src/render/common/comment.ts:4-19.

landing_point.why: The report says TypeScript is injected through a schema, and this is the single place where free-form schema text (description / deprecation reason) is wrapped in `/** ... */` and written into the generated files; every renderer calls it through typeComment/fieldComment/argumentComment.

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI `genql -o <dir> -s <schema.graphql>` / `-e <endpoint>` (cli/src/cli.ts:110) and the exported programmatic API `generate()` (cli/src/index.ts:1); both reach the renderer through clientTasks (cli/src/tasks/clientTasks.ts:74-84)
fix_sites.module_kind: code-generator render helper (TypeScript renderer, cli package)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: None available: there is no sibling or uncovered route, so the only argument a solver could make is that a GraphQL schema is trusted input, which the advisory contradicts by treating the schema as attacker-controlled.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Descriptions are reproduced verbatim in generated output and the renderers depend on the builder's exact layout: each emitted field string is split on newlines and re-indented (requestTypes/objectType.ts:84-90, responseTypes/objectType.ts:47-53), argument comments are joined inline with ', ' (requestTypes/objectType.ts:99-108), and deprecation whitespace is deliberately collapsed to single spaces (comment.ts:8). An over-broad fix that escapes every '/', '*' or backslash, or that switches to one-line/block form, changes generated files such as integration-tests/generated/schema.ts:20 and breaks the existing comment test expectations.
